Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the AeroGlobal Dynamics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, ladies and gentlemen, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Jenkins, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to AeroGlobal Dynamics' Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are David Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Lisa Patel, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-K and 10-Q, for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied in these statements.

David Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. AeroGlobal Dynamics delivered a solid performance in Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio across commercial aerospace, defense systems, and mission services. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering long-term value to our shareholders. Today, I'll highlight our progress in key areas, including major new contract awards and program wins, the strong performance of our priority defense programs, revenue growth by segment, and our profitability metrics. We're particularly excited about the recent advancements in our next-generation hypersonics and F-35 mission systems programs, and their potential to fuel multi-year growth. We are seeing strong demand for our defense capabilities, and our commercial aerospace business is recovering steadily amid OEM production ramps.

I'll now turn it over to Michael to provide deeper insights into these areas and walk through our financial results.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, David, and good morning, everyone. I'm thrilled to dive into our results, starting with the major new contract awards and program wins this quarter, which underscore the strength of our diversified portfolio spanning fixed-wing aircraft, missile defense, space systems, and unmanned platforms. These achievements validate our technical leadership and position us for sustained revenue growth, especially with global defense spending projected at a 5.2% CAGR through 2028 according to Deloitte's latest A&D outlook—driven by great-power competition and near-peer threats.

In tactical aircraft, our crown jewel, we've secured a $4.8 billion Lot 18 low-rate initial production contract from the U.S. Air Force for the F-35 Lightning II Joint Strike Fighter program, where we act as the exclusive mission systems integrator. Announced just last week, it includes full-rate production funding for advanced electronic warfare suites and sensor fusion upgrades with our proprietary AESA radar enhancements, offering 25% improved target discrimination in contested electromagnetic environments. Year-to-date, F-35 bookings total $12.2 billion, up 28% from last year, pushing our program backlog to $42 billion—a 15% sequential increase.

We're also expanding in hypersonics with a $2.1 billion Defense-wide contract under the DoD's Hypersonic and High-Speed Weapon Prototyping program. This five-year IDIQ covers boost-glide vehicle integration and ground-test infrastructure for our ARRW derivative, co-developed with partners like Lockheed Martin. We've exercised $650 million in task orders for Phase 2 flight testing at White Sands, hitting Mach 7+ velocities with 40% reduced thermal signature via novel carbon-carbon composite leading edges. Hypersonics now represent 12% of our R&D spend, up from 7% last year, aligning with the Pentagon's $13.4 billion FY24 request—a 20% year-over-year uplift.

Internationally, demand from NATO allies and Indo-Pacific partners is robust. A key win is our $1.9 billion Foreign Military Sales package to the Polish Ministry of Defense for Patriot Advanced Capability-3 MSE interceptors and integrated fire control networks, including 150 missiles, launcher upgrades, and IBCS interoperability using Raytheon-sourced GEM-T boosters for 30% extended range. This mirrors Europe's rearmament trend, with NATO spending hitting 2% of GDP for 23 allies. We've also signed an $850 million framework agreement with the Australian Defence Force for MQ-9B SkyGuardian UAS sustainment and Loyal Wingman integration under AUKUS Pillar II. International sales now make up 32% of bookings, up from 25% in Q4 last year, with a 1.4x book-to-bill ratio exceeding our 1.1x-1.2x target.

In space and C4ISR, we captured a $1.2 billion Space Development Agency Tranche 2 Transport Layer contract for proliferated low-Earth orbit satellites with optical inter-satellite links. Our 28-satellite constellation, based on Northrop Grumman heritage bus designs, supports 100 Gbps data rates for resilient missile warning in GPS-denied environments. This builds on our $3.5 billion space systems backlog, supported by the FY24 NDAA's $30 billion space budget increase.

Overall, these $11 billion in net new awards—our strongest quarterly since Q1 2020—have grown our funded backlog to $68.4 billion, up 22% year-over-year, offering 3.2 years of coverage at current rates. Program margins average 12.5% EBIT, aided by fixed-price incentives and cost-plus sustainment tails that counter inflation risks from titanium shortages up 18% year-over-year per USGS. We're using digital engineering twins and additive manufacturing to shorten LRIP-to-FRP timelines by 15 months, de-risking NGAD pursuits where we hold digital backbone workshares.

U.S. DoD awards lead at 62%, but Middle East growth at 18%—via UAE THAAD co-production—and Asia-Pacific at 14% offset slower legacy ramps amid Ukraine munitions depletion. This diversifies us from legacy sustainment (now 28% of revenue) toward collaborative combat aircraft and directed energy weapons, where our 300 kW laser demonstrator passed naval qualifications.

Now, shifting to the performance of our priority defense programs, which form the cornerstone of our $28.5 billion backlog—up 18% year-over-year—and drove 22% organic revenue growth in our Defense segment to $4.2 billion this quarter. These efforts advance U.S. and allied deterrence across the Indo-Pacific and Europe.

Our Joint All-Domain Strike portfolio, led by F-35 sustainment and upgrades as a Tier 1 supplier with Lockheed Martin, generated $1.8 billion in Q3 revenue, up 25% year-over-year, from accelerated Block 4 modernizations. We've finished 95% of LRIP Lots 15-17 ahead of schedule by six months using digital twins via Siemens NX and NVIDIA Omniverse for predictive maintenance. This unlocked $2.1 billion in FRP options from the JPO, with margins up 150 basis points to 13.2% from additive manufacturing of titanium engine parts, cutting lead times 40% and scrap below 2%.

In next-generation air dominance, NGAD demonstrator subsystems hit TRL 7, with first-flight on our adaptive cycle engine prototype featuring variable cycle bypass for 30% better fuel efficiency than F135s. We booked $850 million in DARPA ACE R&D funding, aiding 12% segment margins. Backlog is $12.4 billion, on track for FY25 Milestone B amid USAF realignments.

Hypersonics shine with our Dark Eagle boost-glide vehicle for Army Long-Range Hypersonic Weapon integration outperforming targets. Q3 saw 18 flight test articles delivered at 85% success on Mach 5+ glides from White Sands and Kwajalein, surging revenue 35% to $720 million on $3.2 billion multi-year Army contracts. Margins at 11.8% despite composites headwinds, mitigated by dual-sourcing with Hexcel and $150 million reshoring.

Missile defense IAMD suite, including Glide Phase Interceptor work, hit $650 million revenue up 28%, with $9.1 billion backlog from MDA's $1.2 billion Pacific Deterrence award. AI fire control via Palantir Foundry cut sensor-to-shooter times 60% off Guam. FMS to Japan, Australia added $500 million; Poland's Patriot buys accelerated.

Uncrewed systems like MQ-Next loyal wingmen secured $420 million AFWERX contracts, autonomy at TRL 8 after 250 F-35 teaming hours. Space efforts, including HBTSS for SDA, added $380 million up 40% on Tranche 2 SATCOM needs.

Operationally, 15% workforce growth in propulsion via $200 million DoD SkillBridge handles shortages. Inventory at 145 days buffers rhenium and rare earths. NDAA FY25 supplementals could add $100 billion, with us at 14% share per BloombergNG.

These programs show Q3 EBITA margins of 12.9%—200 bps above guidance—and 110% free cash flow conversion. We're raising Defense full-year to $17-18 billion revenue, 12-14% margins for 15%+ CAGR.

Next, our revenue by segment. Consolidated revenues reached $22.4 billion, up 11% year-over-year, from execution in Commercial Aerospace, Defense, and Services—highlighting portfolio resilience amid supply chain normalization and geopolitics.

Commercial Aerospace grew 18% to $12.1 billion, strongest since pre-pandemic. OEM up 25% to $8.7 billion on Boeing 737 MAX/787 nacelles (45 shipsets vs. 32) and Airbus A320neo LEAP-1A kits (50+ units). Narrowbody backlog $145 billion. Aftermarket up 5% to $3.4 billion, disciplined on inflation. North America 55% up 22%; Asia-Pacific 15% on A350s; China cautious at 8%. 'Sustainable Skies' with magniX hybrid-electric demos targets 2030, 12% productivity via digital twins. Mid-teens growth into 2025 with 777X.

Defense at $7.8 billion, +7%, stable on $842 billion DoD FY24 and supplements. Missiles up 14% to $3.2 billion (450 JASSM-ER/LRASM); hypersonics $450 million. Fixed-wing $2.9 billion flat but F-35 upside; rotary/ISR $1.7 billion +9%. U.S. DoD 65% +10%; international 25% +5%. 'Integrated Deterrence' yields $2.1 billion awards; backlog $112 billion +9%.

Services $2.5 billion +12%, 22% margins at 92% utilization. Engines $1.2 billion +15% (CF6/PW4000, GE9X); landing gear $800 million +10%; digital $500 million +25% via AeroLens (1,800 airframes, 18% downtime cut). EMEA +18%, APAC +8%, North America +10%. 'Services 4.0' AI PHM targets 25% revenues by 2027.

Overall, 11% growth, EBIT margins +120 bps to 14.2%. $320 billion backlog +8%, 2.3x book-to-bill. Supply chain 40% non-China.

Finally, profitability: segment-adjusted gross margin 19.8% +140 bps year-over-year on $18.7 billion revenue (wait, aligning to our $22.4 billion consolidated—strong across). Operating margin 13.2% +90 bps; diluted EPS $2.15 +12%. Favorable mix in sustainment/upgrades.

Aeronautics 21.5% +140 bps (42% sales) on F-35 Lot 15 ramp, 95% affordability, $250 million digital thread savings, 18% scrap reduction. Missiles & Space 22.3% +220 bps on JASSM/hypersonics, FMS pricing, dual-sourcing vs. 7% inflation. Rotary dip to 17.2% offset by $120 million adjustments.

U.S. DoD $12.4 billion +8%; international 28% record $5.2 billion, EMEA +15%, APAC steady.

Operating leverage from SG&A 4.1% (down from 4.5%), R&D 6.2%. Absorbed $180 million labor inflation (5.2% industry) via ERP 12% gains. 'Margin Plus' FPD 35% backlog. Classified 15.4%; $45 million C4ISR charge offset by SOSA.

Equity earnings +10% $120 million; interest $85 million, 2.8x leverage. Net income $1.65 billion, tax 21.8% on R&D credits. $75 million drone divestiture minus $30 million titanium write-downs.

Positions for 13-15% margins, $145 billion backlog 40% international, services +22%. FY24 $75-77 billion revenue, 19.5-20% gross, $8.50-8.80 EPS. $500 million supplier pool.

In Q3, we reported revenue of $22.4 billion, an 11% increase year-over-year. Earnings per share were $2.15. We maintain $5.8 billion in cash equivalents. Full-year guidance unchanged; managing costs, investing growth, returning capital via dividends and repurchases.

Highlights: Gross margin 19.8%; operating income $2.96 billion; free cash flow $2.4 billion.

David Reynolds:
Thank you, Michael. These results reflect our team's execution and strategic positioning in a dynamic market.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from John Carter with Barclays. Please go ahead.

John Carter:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the major new contract awards, particularly the F-35 Lot 18 and hypersonics outlook?

David Reynolds:
Certainly, John. The $4.8 billion F-35 LRIP Lot 18 solidifies our role as mission systems lead, with AESA upgrades enhancing contested ops. Hypersonics $2.1 billion IDIQ builds on ARRW successes at Mach 7+, aligning with DoD priorities. Combined with international like Poland's $1.9 billion Patriot, our $11 billion wins boost backlog to $68.4 billion, supporting mid-teens growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Rodriguez:
Hi, thanks. I'm curious about revenue by segment, especially Commercial Aerospace recovery and Defense stability?

Michael Chen:
Emily, Commercial Aerospace's 18% growth to $12.1 billion came from OEM ramps like 45 Boeing nacelles and aftermarket discipline. Defense's 7% to $7.8 billion reflects missiles +14% and steady fixed-wing, with geopolitical tailwinds. Services +12% at high margins rounds it out, with $320 billion backlog visibility.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Kline with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Robert Kline:
Regarding the gross and operating margin expansion—any color on sustainability?

David Reynolds:
Robert, our 19.8% gross and 13.2% operating margins, up 140 and 90 bps, stem from mix shifts to F-35 sustainment, cost-outs like $250 million digital savings, and SG&A control. 'Margin Plus' and supply mitigations position us for 13-15% long-term, even with inflation.

David Reynolds:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our Q3 2024 earnings call. A replay will be available on our investor relations website.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
